After SONA ...whither South Africa ?

By: Jane Lipman | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Democracy under threat ....has Nelson Mandela 's dream faded ?

Summary:
After the State of the Nation chaos Feb 12 , parliament debates the extraordinary events including the armed police in the chamber and jamming of the cell phone signal ....members from all parties explain their way forward and constitutional law experts explain where we stand .....

Further information:
we are requesting to interview Lindi Sisulu/ Zizi Kodwa/ Julius Malema / Musi Maimane / Bantu Holomisa /Pierre De Vos . We will access footage from the debate and Zuma's response on Thursday and ask ..where are we headed as a country ? Are we becoming a police state? Has State Security taken control ? What does this mean for ordinary South Africans ?What does governance mean to South Africans ?Did Jacob Zuma shift the mood last Thursday with his SONA reply ?

Mr. Pierre De Vos

Press Release:


SONA: the aftermath
President Jacob Zuma remains in the eye of the SONA storm. Debate around last week’s address saw opposition parties pull no punches with the president labelled everything from ‘A broken man presiding over a broken society’, to a man telling a so-called good story. Carte Blanche tests the energy of swelling political dissent and asks: can we afford to take the Constitution for granted?


Script:


SCRIPT SONA Fallout

VOICE OVER
In Cape Town late last week there was a mood of reconciliation as Jacob Zuma responded to the State of the Nation debate and went out of his way to praise his critics ,although the opposition still felt many issues remained .
SOUND UP “ Reply by the President to the debate on the State of the Nation Address “
SOUND UP Baleka Mbete “The Honourable the President
SOUND UP Jacob Zuma It is now almost twenty one years since we started the radical transition from colonialism of a special type to a national democratic society founded on the strategic vison of the Freedom Charter .
STAND UP LINK FROM JOHN WEBB The SONA Debacle led some people to say that South Africa is now a broken country but have developments in parliament stifled or invigorated debate?

VOICE OVER Earlier last week opposition parties had criticised the President .
Julius Malema Sound Up “ We ask that President Zuma should go home and rest that is the best solution .

VOICE OVER Julius Malema says the EFF has a mandate from over a million voters to force the President to be accountable
Julius Malema sound up “the man is highly conflicted ,the man has destroyed every credible institution of the State “
VOICE OVER Human Settlements Minister Lindiwe Sisulu speaks for the ANC and denies Zuma must resign.

Lindiwe Sisulu SOUND UP “only the ANC can consider that proposition and at the moment it is preposterous “


VOICE OVER Last Tuesday Musi Maimane said Jacob Zuma was not an honourable man.

Sound Up Mmusi Maimane “Honourable President in these very chambers just five days ago you broke parliament ,please understand Honourable President when I use the term honourable I do it out of respect for the traditions and conventions of this august house but please don’t take it literally …

Lindi Sisulu Sound Up “Every member of parliament is honourable ,deemed honourable and that is how we address people you cant say honourable and say you are dishonourable in fact it is contrary to the rules of parliament that you should impune the character of an honourable member

John Webb stand up Shortly after the State of the Nation address Baleka Mbete called Julius Malema a cockroach and while she was speaking at an ANC meeting at the time opposition parties say that the comment exposes her bias
Julius “Well I Think that was irresponsible of the Speaker to call me a cockroach , given the position of influence she holds

VOICE OVER Then Mbete apologised late on Wednesday ,TO South Africans , to Parliament and Julius Malema withdrawing her remarks unconditionally . Julius Malema accepted her apology . Baleka Mbete only returned to parliament on Thursday .

Julius Sound up she was effectively putting a price tag on my head and calling for assassination of members of the EFF ,because we know what happened to those who were called cockroaches in Rwanda

LINK ON CAMERA John Webb there appeared to be a different atmosphere at SONA 2015 ,a helicopter circled over head and there was increased police presence in and around parliament , that and the violence that followed lead some people to ask the question ,is South Africa becoming a police state ?


Sound Up Bantu Holomisa
Whether its inside the house its clear that we are already a police state ,because Zuma has been running this country using a securocrat mentality right from the word go

VOICE OVER Some believe Zuma has presided over the creation of a South African securocracy including Murray Hunter from the Right to Know campaign
Sound up Murray Hunter We have seen around the Presidents personal political crises the security cluster has been involved every step of the way ,when the Public Protector brought out her report on the expenditure at Nkandla ,it wasn’t the President who took her to court it was Ministers in the Security Cluster ,when MP’s in the EFF disrupted Parliament in November and August of last year it wasn’t the President or parliament who responded to that crisis it was ministers of the Security Cluster that came to parliament to say we are putting in new security measures , we are going to be setting the rules of the game going forward , we have to ask ourselves is that their role are we comfortable with them policing our democracy in this way ?
VOICE OVER
As we know now on February 12 intelligence agencies ,the military , and the police briefed State Security about a carefully laid security plan in case of disruption from the EFF .Constitutional obligations were ignored . EFF members were actively targeted. The DA is still pursuing legal action .But Zuma wants to move on from the fracas .

ZUMA SOUND UP “ You know if you are angry you can say things that you wouldn’t have said if you were not angry ,because you are angry ,once you are angry the capacity to think gets affected

Musi Maimane SOUND UP “It amazes me how South Africans who are constitutionalists see nothing wrong with the fact that there is a jamming device in the house or South Africans who are constitutionalists see nothing wrong that there’ s police coming into the chamber




VOICE OVER
A WEEK LATER JACOB ZUMA SAID THE JAMMING WOULD NOT HAPPEN AGAIN .
HE REPEATED THIS IN A SPECIALLY ARRANGED MEETING WITH THE SOUTH AFRICAN NATIONAL EDITORS FORUM ON FRIDAY





SOUND UP JACOB ZUMA FEB 19 The security cluster has addressed and clarified matters relating to the signal disruption the interference in the house last Thursday ,it is an unfortunate incident ,it should never happen again .


VOICE OVER Pierre De Vos is a Constitutional Law Expert

Pierre De Vos there are attempts like the outrageous and clearly illegal scrambling of the cell phone signal in parliament it suggests that there is an attempt to stop ordinary people from getting the information they need to exercise their vote responsibly

Julius Malema sound up “Parliament owes to all of us ,members of parliament including visitors ,you know they owe to us to protect us but if it is parliament that unleashes terror on us ,if it is parliament that unleashes harassment on members of parliament , then all of us do not feel safe we are going to be scared to speak openly as encouraged by the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa .

VOICE OVER Even though it was a week where order in parliament was restored the opposition parties were unconvinced …
John question on camera “How concerned should ordinary South Africans be?

Mmusi Maimane if nothing seriously turns around we will see institutional decay ,we will see instability on the ground simply because people will lose their work ,that creates a different problem ,we will see increasing levels of that .


SOUND UP Bantu Holomisa “We are talking now about civil disobedience ,in fact if you look at what is happening in the streets there are signs of that we are marching towards a second revolution , once the population rise up and start burning state properties and resist security forces those are signs

Julius Malema “Lets go to the streets President Mandela said if the ANC does to us what the apartheid did to us ,we must do to the ANC what we did to apartheid ,we have reached that point …

Jacob Zuma FINAL SOUND UP Even if we differ I always see no reason why we should get angry ,what for ,this is not war ,we are not fighting ,democracy says be free to express your views and allow the others to express their views as well ,that is democracy



PROMOS


John Webb standup Is Parliament broken and if so what will it take to fix it ? we examine developments in the National Assembly this Sunday on Carte Blanche

VOICE OVER Zuma wanted to bury the hatchet last week but did the opposition buy it ?
VOICE OVER there was a spirit of reconciliation in parliament at the end of last week but will it last ?
